title: Reading FASTA through Reader and FastaParser takes 2 to 6 times as long as needletail

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0eeac819
notes.text:
Progress on the working tree, not yet committed. Medians of 7 interleaved warm runs on an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, under `taskset -c 0-3`, with the issue's harness built against `libsail` by path. "needletail, owned" calls `rec.seq().into_owned()` on every record, so it builds what `parse` builds. Plain needletail borrows a record on one line and never copies it, which is less work than `parse` does.

| input | needletail | needletail, owned | libsail before | libsail now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DNA, wrapped at 60 | 0.373 s | 0.375 s | 0.831 s | 0.367 s |
| DNA, one line per record | 0.137 s | 0.224 s | 0.591 s | 0.261 s |
| protein | 0.492 s | 0.495 s | 0.807 s | 0.433 s |

## What changed

- `parse` hands the residues to a private `append_residues` in `seq/fasta.rs`. It checks each 4 KiB block with `memchr3` for space, tab and form feed. A clean block is copied in the runs between `\n` and `\r` that `memchr2` finds. Any other block goes through the old byte filter. The per-byte filter was 71 to 81% of samples before.
- `Reader` builds its memmem `Finder` once. `memmem::find` built one on every call, which was 38% of framing time on protein.
- `Reader::fill` keeps only the bytes from the cursor on for an initiating format. It no longer moves the previous record before each read. That move was about 87 ms on the wrapped DNA file. After a failed `advance`, a FASTA reader's `record()` is empty.

## Tried and removed

- Finding FASTA's `>` with `memchr` and checking for a newline before it, in place of memmem on `\n>`. Framing alone gained about 2 ms on 1 GiB, which is within noise. Scanning a 44 MB buffer seems bound by memory bandwidth whichever search runs, but nobody has measured that.
- A `libsail` function that appends a record's residues to a buffer the caller owns. It would let a caller skip `parse`, and would not make `parse` any faster.

## Open

- One-line DNA trails owned needletail by about 0.04 s. Not yet placed.
- The last open item in the body points at sail-56ab6e, which was closed as dropped.

Harness, inputs, perf data and timing logs are in `tmp-claude/2026-11-19-fasta-gap/`, which is not committed.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0eeac819
notes.text:
Ways to go below needletail, measured in `tmp-claude/2026-11-19-fasta-gap/repro/src/floors.rs` and not adopted. Medians of 5 warm runs, same machine and harness as the note above, single thread unless stated.

| variant | DNA wrapped | DNA one line | protein |
|---|---|---|---|
| needletail | 0.383 s | 0.139 s | 0.507 s |
| `Reader` and `parse` | 0.366 s | 0.264 s | 0.455 s |
| mmap and `parse` | 0.284 s | 0.175 s | 0.385 s |
| mmap, residues copied straight into the caller's text | 0.231 s | 0.122 s | 0.311 s |
| mmap, 4 threads, count then copy into one text | 0.139 s | 0.120 s | 0.169 s |
| one fused AVX-512 pass over mmap, `vpcompressb` | 0.249 s | 0.194 s | 0.269 s |

Every variant produced byte-identical text.

- mmap saves the kernel's copy from the page cache into the read buffer, about 0.08 s per GiB with a warm cache. Nobody has measured it cold, where the disk should dominate. It cannot read a pipe or gzip.
- Copying into a buffer the caller owns saves the write into `FastaRecord::seq`, 0.05 to 0.07 s. This is the shape sail-56ab6e proposed.
- A fused single pass is no faster than the `memchr` runs, even with the file already in memory (0.14 to 0.18 s). Passes over bytes still in cache cost little. The cost is trips to main memory.
- needletail leads on one-line records because `SequenceRecord::seq` returns `Cow::Borrowed` from its read buffer when the sequence holds no `\r` or `\n`. `FastaRecord` owns its residues, so `parse` always writes them. A borrowing record type would close that row.

Jack decided against all four API changes for now: a reader over a mapped file, a residue copy into a caller's buffer, a parallel read, and a borrowing record. Within the current API, the remaining one-line gap of about 0.035 s against owned needletail is mostly the framing scan reading a 44 MB record after it has left the cache. Bounded reads with a remembered scan position would recover an estimated 25 ms on that input alone, and were judged not worth the code.
